ClientSessionContext attributes are transient wrappers around client session notes in DefaultClientSessionContext; whether the attribute is persisted depends on the implementation writing it back to the AuthenticatedClientSessionModel notes. If it is not persisted, a later refresh of the token will read the attribute from a freshly-loaded client session context and get null, encoding 'na' instead of the original grant type. The grant type should be stored via clientSession.setNote(...) (the persisted mechanism) or the persistence behavior of setAttribute must be confirmed and relied upon consistently (TokenManager's refresh path reads it via clientSessionCtx.getAttribute, so both write and read must use the same mechanism).

findings.title: Unit test bypasses factory postInit and hand-builds internal maps, so it does not test real wiring
findings.body: The test constructs DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, calls init(null), then directly assigns package-private fields grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts with a hand-built map, bypassing postInit entirely. This means the test does not exercise the real grant-type discovery/registration logic (postInit iterating OAuth2GrantType factories, duplicate validation, UNKNOWN registration), nor the lazy-refresh paths in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut (sessionFactory is null, so those paths would NPE if hit). Tests for duplicate shortcut detection, unknown-grant fallback during encoding, and decoding of ids with wrong prefix length are also missing.

findings.title: encodeTokenId throws for grant type 'na' (UNKNOWN) because the UNKNOWN grant is registered under the literal string 'na', not under itself as a grant type
findings.body: In getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext, when no grant type attribute is present, grantType is set to the literal string "na" (UNKNOWN). encodeTokenId then calls factory.getShortcutByGrantType("na"). In postInit, the maps are populated with grantsToShortcuts.put("na", "na"), so this resolves — but only if postInit ran and registered it. However, the AccessTokenContext constructor requires a non-null grantType and the UNKNOWN constant is the shortcut, not a grant type URI; any custom TokenContextEncoderProvider or any path where the maps were refreshed (lazy refresh path in getShortcutByGrantType looks up sessionFactory.getProviderFactory(OAuth2GrantType.class, "na") which returns null, then re-reads the map) is fragile. More concretely: the semantics conflate 'unknown grant type' with the shortcut value 'na'; if a deployment's maps are refreshed or a custom factory overrides the maps, encoding a token with unknown grant type throws IllegalStateException and breaks token issuance. encodeTokenId should explicitly map the UNKNOWN grant to the UNKNOWN shortcut instead of relying on map contents.
